preArrival.simple: Compare Google Flights or Skyscanner with Brazil-focused Decolar, then book/check the operating airline. Brazil is large: choose an airport for the actual region you plan to visit.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Brasília (BSB) is a central hub; São Paulo (GRU/CGH), Rio (GIG/SDU), and other regional airports serve different itineraries. Use Google Flights/Skyscanner for broad comparisons and Decolar for Brazil-focused booking; verify baggage, airport, and connection terms with the airline.

Entry rules: Visa and eVisa requirements depend on nationality, passport, purpose, and date. Check Brazil's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and consular guidance before payment; do not infer eligibility from an OTA listing.

Climate and packing: Brazil spans equatorial, tropical, highland, and subtropical climates. Check the weather for each state and season; pack sun/rain protection and light layers.

sources.topic: Brazil Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular portal

arrival24h.simple: Brazil uses Type N sockets; voltage is commonly 127 or 220 V at 60 Hz depending on location. PIX is widely used, but visitor access depends on a Brazilian account/provider.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: Type N sockets; 127/220 V at 60 Hz, depending on city and property. Check appliance input labels and the accommodation's local supply. A plug adapter does not convert voltage.

Connectivity and payments: Confirm roaming/eSIM coverage with your carrier. PIX is ubiquitous domestically, but visitors may not be able to register without local banking access; retain an international card and some BRL cash.

Arrival transfer: Airports and city transport differ widely. Check the airport's official ground-transport page, use marked taxi/ride-hailing pickup points, and confirm the fare and destination before leaving.

mobility.simple: Brasília relies on metro and buses; other cities have their own systems. For intercity travel, compare airline routes with bus operators such as ClickBus.
mobility.detailed:
Brasília: Metro-DF and city buses connect major districts; confirm route, hours, and ticket options with the operator. Distances and superblocks make some journeys longer on foot than the map suggests.

Other cities and long-distance travel: São Paulo, Rio, and other capitals have distinct metro/BRT systems. Compare flights with coach routes and current bus operators; confirm the departure terminal and baggage rules.

Ride-hailing: Uber and 99 are common in many urban areas, but coverage varies. Check the registered plate and pickup point in-app; use marked crossings and account for heat and uneven sidewalks.

dailyLiving.simple: iFood and Rappi cover many urban addresses; check the exact zone. PIX, tap water, pharmacies, and comida por quilo practices vary by location and venue.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery and shopping: iFood and Rappi are widely used in larger cities; enter the exact address and check phone/payment requirements. Mercado Livre is a major marketplace, but delivery times depend on region.

Food and payment: PIX is a domestic instant-payment rail; use only a payment method you can lawfully register. Comida por quilo restaurants charge by weight; check how tare is handled and the posted price per kilogram.

Health and water: Tap-water quality and infrastructure vary by municipality/building. Ask locally and use sealed or treated water if uncertain. Bring prescriptions in original packaging and verify import rules.

socialCode.simple: Portuguese is the national language. Ask before photographing people; follow local cues on greetings, footwear, religious sites, and shared dining.
socialCode.detailed:
Greetings and language: Brazilian Portuguese is used nationwide, with regional variation. A friendly greeting is common, but physical contact preferences differ; follow the other person's lead.

Home and dining: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether to bring something for the host. At shared meals, ask about dietary needs and follow the host's serving style.

Photography: Ask permission before photographing people, homes, or ceremonies. Follow posted rules at religious and heritage sites; avoid broad claims about one national etiquette.

preArrival.simple: Direct booking on Mexican carriers. Visa-free for many (FMM form). Varied climate: CDMX 12°C to 26°C, Cancún 22°C to 33°C. Casual dress, modest for churches.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight Consolidators & Hub Routing: MEX (Mexico City), CUN (Cancún), GDL (Guadalajara) major hubs. Aeroméxico (flag carrier), Volaris, VivaAerobus budget carriers. Direct booking typical. No regional consolidator standard.

Visa & Legal Compliance: Visa-free for 65+ countries (US, Canada, EU, UK, Japan). FMM (Forma Migratoria Múltiple) required for all (free at airport, valid 180 days). Visa required for others. Passport valid 6 months beyond stay.

Climate & Weather: Varied by altitude/region. Mexico City: 12°C (Jan) to 26°C (July). Cancún: 22°C to 33°C. Guadalajara: 11°C to 28°C. Check specific destination. Altitude affects temperature (CDMX 2,240m). Rainy season May-Oct.

Apparel Sourcing: Casual acceptable. Modest dress for churches (no shorts, cover shoulders). Beach culture in coastal areas. Size system: US sizing. Sun protection essential.

arrival24h.simple: Power: 127V, 60Hz, Type A/B sockets. 4G/5G good, eSIM available. NFC contactless growing. Authorized taxi booths at airports.
arrival24h.detailed:
Electrical Infrastructure: 127V, 60Hz (some areas 220V). Type A (two flat pins) and Type B (two flat + ground pin) sockets. Visual reference: https://www.power-plugs-sockets.com/type-a/

Connectivity & ISP: Average broadband 50+ Mbps. 4G coverage 92%, 5G in cities. ISPs: Telcel, Movistar, AT&T Mexico. Tourist eSIM: Airalo, Holafly. Local SIM: Telcel (~$40/week).

Financial Rails: NFC contactless growing (SPEI system). Cash still widely used. No mobile money. Tipping: 10-15% expected in restaurants, round up for services.

Airport-to-City: Mexico City MEX: Authorized taxi only (airport booth, ~$25-35 to center). Metro Line 5 (₺5, 30min). Cancún: ADO bus ($12, 30min) or authorized taxi (~$35-50). Never use unauthorized taxis at airports.

mobility.simple: CDMX Metro (12 lines), Metrobus (BRT). Pesero (informal minibuses). Uber, Didi ride-hailing. Ecobici bike share. Walkability: good in centers, security concerns.
mobility.detailed:
Urban Transit Grids: Mexico City: 12 Metro lines, Metrobus BRT, trolleybus. Integrated card: Metrobús card. Guadalajara: SITE, Macrobus. Monterrey: Metrorrey. Apps: CDMX Mobility, Moovit.

Informal Transit: Pesero (informal minibuses) operating fixed routes, frequent but unregulated. Colectivos (shared taxis) common. Informal transit significant in cities.

Micro-Mobility & Ride-Hailing: Uber, Didi dominant. No Bolt. Bike-sharing: Ecobici (CDMX), MiBici (GDL). E-scooters: Grin, Spin in CDMX.

Pedestrian Infrastructure: Variable. Excellent in Polanco, Roma, Condesa. Crowded in historic center. Security concerns in some areas at night. Sidewalk quality varies. Pedestrian crossings: use zebra crossings, cars may not yield.

dailyLiving.simple: Delivery: Rappi, Didi Food, Uber Eats. Alcohol: supermarket sales, no restrictions. Pharmacy: many OTC, antibiotics Rx. Tap water: not safe - boil or bottle.
dailyLiving.detailed:
E-Commerce & Delivery: Dominant: Rappi (Colombian, extensive), Didi Food, Uber Eats. Local: Cornershop (grocery). Grocery delivery: Walmart, Chedraui. 24/7 Rappi delivery culture.

Retail & Alcohol: Open sales in supermarkets, convenience stores (OXXO). No state monopoly. Drinking age 18. Tequila/mezcal culture. Tipping expected.

Pharmacy: Many OTC medications. Antibiotics Rx-only (enforced). Pharmacies: Farmacias del Ahorro, Benavides. Farmacias Similares (generic). 24h pharmacies common.

Beverage & Dietary: **Tap water not safe** - boil or use bottled water. Zero-sugar options available. Local: Coca-Cola (very popular), aguas frescas. Corn tortillas, beans, chiles staple.

Buffet Protocols: Hotel buffets: multi-plate common. Traditional: one-plate with refills. Comida corrida (set menu) common. Sharing dishes typical. No restrictions on refills.

socialCode.simple: Gifts: avoid yellow marigolds (death), wine/food OK. Shoes removed in some homes. Dog-friendly in cities. Hospitality, family focus, personal space moderate.
socialCode.detailed:
Gift-Giving Etiquette: Flowers: avoid yellow marigolds (associated with death). Odd numbers preferred. Wine, tequila, regional food appropriate. Host gifts expected for dinner.

Household Norms: Shoes often removed in homes. Follow host's lead.

Companion Pet Culture: Dog-friendly in cities, less in rural areas. Dogs in restaurants (patios). Stray dogs common in rural areas. Cat culture present.

Behavioral Matrix: Collectivist, family-focused. Warm, expressive culture. Physical greetings: handshake (formal), hug/kiss on cheek (friends). Punctuality: 30-60 min grace socially (mañana culture). Tipping: 10-15% expected. Personal space moderate. Siesta tradition fading but late lunches (2-4pm) common.

preArrival.simple: No consolidator needed - direct booking. ESTA visa waiver (€14) or B1/B2 visa. Varied climate: check destination. Casual dress, beach to business formal.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight Consolidators & Hub Routing: Major hubs: JFK/LGA/EWR (NYC), LAX (LA), ORD (Chicago), ATL (Atlanta), DFW (Dallas). Direct booking typical. No regional consolidator standard. Delta, American, United legacy carriers; Southwest, JetBlue budget.

Visa & Legal Compliance: Visa Waiver Program (ESTA) for 38 countries - 90 days, €14 online. Otherwise B1/B2 tourist visa required. Passport valid 6 months beyond stay. TSA PreCheck/Global Entry programs for frequent travelers.

Climate & Weather: Extremely varied by region. Northeast: -5°C to 30°C. Southwest: 10°C to 40°C. Florida: 15°C to 32°C. Check specific destination. Pack layers for cross-country travel.

Apparel Sourcing: Highly varied by region and context. Business casual in cities, casual elsewhere. Beach culture in coastal areas. Religious sites: modest dress. Size system: US sizing differs (shoes, clothing).

arrival24h.simple: Power: 120V, 60Hz, Type A/B sockets (flat pins). 4G/5G excellent, eSIM from Airalo/T-Mobile. NFC ubiquitous (Apple/Google Pay). Uber/Lyft everywhere.
arrival24h.detailed:
Electrical Infrastructure: 120V, 60Hz. Type A (two flat pins) and Type B (two flat + ground pin) sockets. Type A without ground, Type B with ground. Visual reference: https://www.power-plugs-sockets.com/type-a/

Connectivity & ISP: Average broadband 150+ Mbps. 4G coverage 99%, 5G expanding. ISPs: Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile. Tourist eSIM: Airalo, T-Mobile. Local SIM: T-Mobile Prepaid (~$50/month).

Financial Rails: NFC contactless payment universal. Venmo, Zelle, Cash App for P2P. Credit cards essential (Amex, Visa, MC). Cash still used but declining. Tipping: 15-20% expected.

Airport-to-City: Varies widely by city. NYC: AirTrain + subway ($11.75) or taxi/Uber ($50-70). LA: FlyAway bus ($9.75) or rideshare ($40-80). Public transit quality varies significantly by city.

mobility.simple: Varies: NYC subway excellent, LA car-dependent. Uber/Lyft dominant ride-hailing. Lime/Bird e-scooters. Walkability: high in Northeast, low in Sun Belt.
mobility.detailed:
Urban Transit Grids: Highly variable. NYC: Extensive subway/bus system (MTA). DC: Metro (WMATA). Chicago: 'L' trains. LA: Metro (limited). San Francisco: BART/Muni. Many cities: car-dependent. Transit apps: Citymapper, Transit.

Informal Transit: Limited formal alternatives. Some unofficial shuttles in specific markets, but formal systems dominate.

Micro-Mobility & Ride-Hailing: Uber and Lyft nationwide. Lime, Bird, Spin e-scooters in cities. Citi Bike (NYC), Divvy (Chicago), Bay Wheels (SF) bike shares. Car-sharing: Zipcar, Turo.

Pedestrian Infrastructure: Extremely variable. NYC, Boston, SF: highly walkable. LA, Houston, Phoenix: car-dependent, poor walkability. Sidewalk quality varies. ADA compliance required but inconsistent.

dailyLiving.simple: Delivery: DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub dominant. Alcohol: supermarket sales (age 21). Pharmacy: OTC limited, many Rx-only. Tap water safe. Buffet: AYCE multi-plate.
dailyLiving.detailed:
E-Commerce & Delivery: Dominant: DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub. Local: Postmates. Grocery delivery: Instacart, Amazon Fresh. 24/7 delivery culture in major cities.

Retail & Alcohol: Open sales in supermarkets, liquor stores (21+ ID required). No state monopoly except Pennsylvania (limited). Drinking age 21 strictly enforced. Tipping culture pervasive.

Pharmacy: Limited OTC compared to Europe. Many medications Rx-only (antibiotics, strong painkillers). Pharmacies: CVS, Walgreens, Rite Aid. 24h pharmacies common.

Beverage & Dietary: Tap water safe nationwide. Zero-sugar sodas abundant. Local: Dr Pepper, Mountain Dew. Large portion sizes standard. Ice in drinks default.

Buffet Protocols: AYCE (All-You-Can-Eat) multi-plate standard. Refills unlimited. No one-plate restrictions. Hotel buffets: self-serve, multiple plates typical.

socialCode.simple: Gifts: wine, flowers, food items. Shoes usually kept on. Dog-friendly (varies by state). Personal space, direct eye contact, tipping mandatory, casual greetings.
socialCode.detailed:
Gift-Giving Etiquette: Flowers: any number acceptable. Chrysanthemums sometimes associated with death. Wine, regional food, gift cards appropriate. Host gifts appreciated but not mandatory.

Household Norms: Shoes typically kept on, unless requested otherwise. Socks expected if shoes removed.

Companion Pet Culture: Dog-friendly but varies by state/city. Many restaurants allow patios, not indoors. Service dog rights protected. Stray dogs rare in cities.

Behavioral Matrix: Individualistic culture. Large personal space. Direct eye contact valued. Firm handshake greetings. Punctuality: socially 10-15 min grace, business on-time. Tipping: 15-20% mandatory in restaurants, taxis, personal services. Casual dress in many settings. Sunglasses acceptable in many contexts.
